The greater majority of those were NGS based products, so that enables our NGS growth. We haven't actually reported the actual contribution that new products actually have delivered within the strategy, but naturally, it's a clear component that's driving the growth within the NGS that we've reported.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. Remember, we launched our. When we say 13, many of those were small.
Mason Carrico
Research Analyst, Stephens
Mm-hmm.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
We're not significant, but, you know, they filled the gap. I would say the ones to think about is in really Q2 of 2023, we launched the new large panel solid, and then in Q3 we did the new large panel heme. That's why I talked about the
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Yeah
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
The comparables as we got into the Q4. Our view is that we need to launch several kind of line extension smaller products each year, but really one to two major products every probably 12 to 18 months. You're gonna see the liquid biopsy come out this year. You'll see really a line extension on our already large panel with HRD. Then really it's in the H1 of 2026 when we'll launch another significant new panel. Think about it that way. It's probably every 12 to 18 months if I take the comparables. As Warren mentioned, we don't break out individually the products. We do break out obviously individually NGS, and most of these products roll into NGS.
Mason Carrico
Research Analyst, Stephens
Okay.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Um-
Mason Carrico
Research Analyst, Stephens
Sorry if I missed this, but have you guys started to see any benefit from the biomarker legislation? What are your expectations around that this year? Is that baked into the guide at all or would that be upside?
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah, it's part of our overall RCM, you know, strategic reimbursement initiatives. I would say it's been slow. I mean, I think just-
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
It's early days.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Just because the legislation is passed does not mean the payers flip a switch and start paying us. I'd still kinda describe it as hand-to-hand combat in the trenches, because you still have to kinda work with each payer in states where it happened, and you're operating with payers that are operating in 50 states that have multiple different payment systems. It's a pretty complex process, but we think it's definitely going to be a tailwind long term, and it's part of the incremental opportunity we see over the next several years to have more of these large panel tests, you know, being required to be paid for by the biomarker legislation.
Mason Carrico
Research Analyst, Stephens
Got it. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question is from Tejas Savant with Morgan Stanley.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Hey, guys. Good morning.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
How you doing?
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Good. How are you? Chris, I wanna go back to, you know, the point about using your channel to push through, you know, partner assays. I think, Jeff, you pointed to Adaptive as one example, but there's other similar activity that's being spurred by that announcement. Can you talk a little bit about what's your long-term philosophy about the shared economics of those arrangements? And more specifically, can you share a little bit more color on how you plan to rejig Salesforce incentives on your end, to ensure a balanced focus for situations where there may be partial overlap with your own assays? I think the Adaptive case was unique in that sense. It's largely sort of complementary.
You know, in a field like MRD, you could envision sort of overlapping, you know, customer bases and value propositions. Just some clarity on that would be great.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah, look, I think the Adaptive, you're right, was very unique in the sense that it's additive. I would say that the majority of the things that we are looking at in licensing. We're probably looking at more in licensing than we are strategic partnerships, but they would be relevant to our current portfolio. They wouldn't probably compete. Because you got to remember, in MRD, there's multiple ways to look at it, you know, whether it's tumor-naive or tumor-informed, things like that. I think we feel pretty good. As far as our field organization, we shift based on where we are trying to drive behaviors.
Morgan can talk more about this, but if you look at the folks that are living more in the oncology clinical setting, they are more incentivized on kind of non-hospital products. Think about heavily weighted on NGS type of things, where the hospital group is probably more incentivized on hospital-based products. I think as we bring these products out, it depends on how we establish that. I mean, we don't publicly disclose how we do that, but we feel very good on the ability to steer the field organization where we feel like they need to spend their time. Yeah. I don't think. I'm looking at Kareem, and maybe Kareem can jump in.
Kareem Saad
Head of Strategy and Transformation, NeoGenomics
Yeah, I mean, I think.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
We're exploring a large number of things. I don't know that any of them are gonna-
Kareem Saad
Head of Strategy and Transformation, NeoGenomics
Yeah, I think one of the key strategic drivers for these partnerships is that there are products and capabilities that are complementary to our existing product set.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Thank you.
Kareem Saad
Head of Strategy and Transformation, NeoGenomics
Our customers are looking for a provider of comprehensive testing across the board.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Easy to do business with.
Kareem Saad
Head of Strategy and Transformation, NeoGenomics
Right.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
They want to do this.
Kareem Saad
Head of Strategy and Transformation, NeoGenomics
For us, that's really the main criteria that drives a lot of these partnerships. We try to minimize the overlap intentionally and deliberately.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah.
Kareem Saad
Head of Strategy and Transformation, NeoGenomics
That's the whole point.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
I think coming back to one of the comments that Kareem made earlier, you know, in the strategic rationale, call point overlap is something that's imperative. I would struggle at this stage to find to support an opportunity that would drive our commercial organization to a different call point, which would then significantly dilute the efforts from a core business perspective. That comes back to sort of how we select these deals.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Got it. That's actually super helpful. I have a quick follow-up really for Jeff on the guide. I think in Q1, at the midpoint, Jeff, you're calling for about 3% EBITDA margins. The full year is around 8%. You talked about the ramp, you know, upfront OpEx backend loaded on revenue. Where are you thinking about sort of exit rates for EBITDA margin in Q4 this year? And is it fair to model that as a jumping off point for 2026? Or should we think of a slight sort of Q1 reset off of which it starts building again with a year-over-year increase next year?
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I think from a trending perspective, Q1 is clearly our weakest quarter. If you go back four or five years, it's always been the weakest quarter of the year. If you look back at last year, you know, Q1 was about a little bit shy of 9% of Adjusted EBITDA for the year, and then the Adjusted EBITDA built and the margin improved throughout the year. I would expect kind of a similar dynamic in 2025 with Q1, you know, being our weakest quarter. You know, I said in that 8% to 10 range. You know, we are increasing some investment in sales expansion enablement, as well as R&D, you know, as I said in my prepared remarks.
We do think, as you have those sales people ramping throughout the year, you'll see more backend benefit from that as well.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Yeah. I wanna make sure I understood, but you're also talking about the jump off from 2025, or were you talking about the gross margin jump off at 2025 into 2026 or the Adjusted EBITDA?
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
I would say.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Adjusted EBITDA.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I would say you will see a similar dynamic, I think, play out because of the seasonality of the business. You'll see a Q4 exit rate. I would expect it will decline, you know, in Q1 2026, and then build again throughout the year just because of the nature of the business.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Right. Be up against Q1 of 2025.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Correct.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Right.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Right.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
It's kind of that stairstep type of thing.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I mean, we do face, you know, some of the high deductible dynamics that others in the industry have talked about as, you know, patients kind of race to see treatment in the Q4 of the year, and then there's kind of a, you know, a little bit of a slowdown in Q1, and you can have more weather impact in Q1 as well, so.
Tejas Savant
Executive Director and Senior Healthcare Equity Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Got it. Fair enough. Thank you, guys.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Thanks.
Operator
Your next question for today is from Mark Massaro with BTIG.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Hey, Mark.
[Analyst] (BTIG)
Analyst, BTIG
Hey, guys. Hey, this is actually Vivian on for Mark. Thanks for taking the questions. A lot has been asked, so I'll just keep it to one maybe. Just the latest on RaDaR V2. It sounds like you may have an inclination to keep pursuing V2 over inorganic growth. Could you just explain your latest thinking around investing in V2 versus M&A? Thanks.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I think you're talking about what we're calling our next-gen, you know, RaDaR. Look, we're gonna go down both avenues. I mean, I just think because of our deep understanding and insight into how to develop those products, a lot of that, our internal stuff, has historically been tumor-informed, so we haven't spent as much time on the research side on tumor-naive. I think. Look, I would say that we're pursuing both opportunities. Look, I wanna be really clear because we're talking a lot about new products. Look, there is a lot of development going on organically, but on the inorganic, we are not going out and buying companies that are not accretive. This isn't a strategy that we're gonna go buy Inivata.
We're gonna go buy some great MRD product that loses $50 million a year. These are very rifle shot, mainly insourced licensing, where companies have innovative technologies, and we may be looking at one or two disease states to be able to take onto that product, and be able to offer it.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
I just wanted to be clear on that.
[Analyst] (BTIG)
Analyst, BTIG
Yes, understood. Thanks for taking the question.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Thanks.
Operator
Your next question is from Matt Sykes at Goldman Sachs.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Hey, Matt.
Prashant Kota
Healthcare Equity Research Senior Associate, Goldman Sachs
Hey, guys. This is Prashant Kota for Matt. Thanks for taking the question. So you mentioned in your slides, 51% improvement in the Gartner Productivity Index on the clinical services side. Can you just talk about the drivers there and how you maintain innovation to stay competitive given your lower R&D spend as a percentage of sales relative to your competitors?
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. It's kinda two different things, but I'm gonna let Warren talk about the Gartner index.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Yeah. It is two different things. One of the things that we started to do going back in, well, when I first started, so late 2022, early 2023, was to assess the sort of maturity and the productivity of our commercial organization. Because we're looking to invest there, but if you haven't got a high productivity, it's kind of you're throwing good money after bad in many instances. There's a standardized assessment that Gartner makes available that measures the productivity of commercial organization. Through that measurement, you're able to identify areas where your productivity is lacking or productivity leaks. We have systematically gone after addressing those leaks, and we continue to do so. We've still got a road ahead of us.
Ultimately, through back office investments in resources, the investments in new systems and tools, and also investments in standardized sales process have been the sort of three key things that we've invested in over the last 2+ years that's allowed for this 50% productivity improvement. This is important because, as we're layering on additional resources, which gives us additional reach, but those resources, the existing resources, are also more productive. It's sort of a compounding effect in terms of the impact that we have within the marketplace. Obviously, you layer on new products that we've been launching from an R&D perspective that we spoke about earlier, and that really fuels the growth. The combination of innovation and increased productivity is what's been driving the growth within the organization.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Thanks.
Prashant Kota
Healthcare Equity Research Senior Associate, Goldman Sachs
Got it. That's helpful. Could you just talk about some of the reasons why providers or health systems would not want NGS-based testing, and how are you looking to overcome those barriers?
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Would not. Nate's on the call.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Yeah.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Maybe if you wanna provide.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Dr. Montgomery, yeah.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Dr. Montgomery could provide a medical perspective on that.
Yeah. You know, I think in general, the trend is that we're seeing less and less of that. The movement is definitely towards panel testing. I think NGS is increasingly incorporated into guidelines. Of course, there are going to be situations where costs could drive a desire in particular circumstances to take a more focused approach. The trend is certainly moving more and more away from that, and I think we would all expect it to continue in that regard. There are a handful of other circumstances where perhaps, again, where there's a particular biomarker of interest where there could be some benefits of sensitivity from a more focused assay. Again, this will increasingly be a smaller and smaller slice of all molecular testing occurring in the oncology space.
Prashant Kota
Healthcare Equity Research Senior Associate, Goldman Sachs
Amazing. Thank you.
Operator
Your next question is from Mike Matson with Needham.
[Analyst] (Needham)
Analyst, Needham
Hi, everybody. This is Joseph.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Hey, how's it going?
[Analyst] (Needham)
Analyst, Needham
Fine.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Yeah.
[Analyst] (Needham)
Analyst, Needham
Good, good. Thank you. I guess I'll just ask my two questions together, if that's all right. The 2028 target to, you know, 1 million patients served, I guess just maybe trying to understand how this matches up with the revenue target. I mean, just based off of, you know, some loose math, it's somewhere around like 9% volume growth to get you to the 1 million patients. Is that how we should kinda think of it as like a base case, high single digits, something like that, 9%, 10% volume growth and the rest coming from, you know, pricing improvements? The second question real quick. NeoComprehensive, you know, launching there with HRD, this year.
Is that something that, you know, clinicians have been kind of asking a lot about that's maybe limiting NeoComprehensive growth? Should we be kinda thinking this is maybe some type of inflection or more of just like an incremental add-on to the test?
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I'll start on the 1 million patients. I would say, you know, that that's, you know, a goal we're, you know, looking at kind of at a macro level, but it also includes pharma patients. It's a little bit of apples and oranges in terms of the patient mix. I wouldn't use that to, you know, drive a volume growth projection on the long range plan. I think, you know, as we continue to build out our sales force, it's gonna be. I think at the end of the day, it's gonna be, as it has been, a continued mixture of both. Both volume growth and increases in revenue driven by higher value tests, RCM initiatives, and pricing gains.
I would say, you know, it's been kind of a balanced approach between the two, maybe a little more heavily weighted on the volume growth side over the last, you know, two years. I wouldn't extrapolate on the million patients to try and, you know, discern a volume number.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
On the HRD question, I think this comes back a little bit to what Dr. Montgomery was saying earlier in that.
You know, the guidelines are changing and HRD is now designed to become more prevalent in guidelines. Today, it's in place for ovarian, and we anticipate prostate and breast to follow in the near future. As a result, this is definitely a need that we see coming from ordering physicians that up until today we're not able to address. This will, when we launch this product early in the H2 of the year, address an unmet need within our portfolio today.
[Analyst] (Needham)
Analyst, Needham
Okay, great. Yeah, super helpful. Thank you for taking our questions.
Operator
Your next question for today is from Dan Brennan with TD Cowen.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Hey, Dan.
Daniel Brennan
Senior Equity Research Analyst and Managing Director, TD Cowen
Great. Thank you. Hey, good morning. Thanks for taking the questions. Maybe the first one just on the advanced diagnostics business, since I know that was kind of the weak spot in the quarter. If you go back to Q3, I know management sounded pretty positive about the business bottoming, and I know you cited no flush as a culprit this quarter. Just kind of wondering if you could dig in a little bit here. I know you talked about a new go-to-market, sounded pretty positive about building a robust pipeline of opportunities back at Q3. Any more color on kind of what's happening on the ground and kind of what does the backlog look like? And when you say grow in 2025, are we thinking like low single-digit growth? Is that the right way to think about it?
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. Maybe let me kind of address it. Look, we obviously talked about that pharma flush. Look, I would definitely say that we feel significantly better going into this year than I think coming out of probably last year. I think when we went from Q3, kind of moving into Q4, we thought we'd get that flush. We don't really report anymore on bookings, but I will tell you that we're having significantly more activity than we would've in this time last year. I think all the trends look good.
Yeah. It was up sequentially, Dan. It wasn't up as much as we expected to be Q3 to Q4. That budget flush has been pretty, I mean, pretty much very consistent over the last multiple years, and we just didn't see it. What I would say, as Chris said, the activity starting out the year has given us, you know, a view that, you know, we should see growth. I think, again, you know, coming off of the non-clinical business being down 7% last year and 12% in Q4, you know, we expect there to be growth. You know, seeing modest growth there is what I would expect is gonna help the overall growth trajectory given the continued strong performance of clinical.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I mean, the challenge here is the long sales cycle. This is a much longer sales cycle to convert from sort of creating bookings to actually convert those bookings into revenue, particularly in prospective studies where they need to obviously enroll patients to get samples, those types of things. It is a long sales cycle, and that's going to hamper the ability in terms of how quickly we can turn this around. We remain very confident in the business.
Daniel Brennan
Senior Equity Research Analyst and Managing Director, TD Cowen
Great. Thanks for that. Maybe just kind of a high-level one on the clinical business. You know, sequencing, I think in your deck said it grew 34% for the year. You guys still have a bunch of products coming out this year which support continued really strong growth. I'm just wondering, like we're coming out with like 32% sequencing growth this year with 4% core. Just wondering if you can comment at all on kind of those assumptions or if not, maybe just on the core side, like, you know, kind of how did the year end up and any way to think about what the right trajectory is for that business in 2025.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah, the way to think about it, Dan, is that we see kinda the modalities. Put NGS aside. We would say that modalities are, we are seeing generally growing 3% to 4, and we've talked that we will grow. We have been, and we project to continue to grow faster than the market.
I think the way we look at NGS is that NGS in the marketplace is growing anywhere from 15% to 20. The same thing, we project it will continue to grow significantly faster than the market. I think that's kind of the clarity that we've given. I don't know, Jeff, if you want to share anything more, but I think that's the way we kind of think about it. That's the reason we like that really is if you're moving the modalities, the lower modalities, you're moving share. I think everybody gets into this NGS growth of the market and everybody's excited. You know, we've you know, John Doe did 100 last year, he'll do 120 this year of NGS. Great.
We also focus significantly on moving share, and I think that's one of the places that we continue to win. That's why we think there's other modalities growing more than market. That's why we call it out, is we think that's a good indicator.
Daniel Brennan
Senior Equity Research Analyst and Managing Director, TD Cowen
Great. Thank you, Chris.
Operator
Your next question is from Andrew Cooper with Raymond James.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Hey, Andrew.
Andrew Cooper
Equity Research Analyst, Raymond James
Hey. Hey, everybody. Thanks for the time. A lot already asked, but maybe just digging in a little bit more, kind of linked to something you just touched on. As we think about that pace of clinical ASP or AUP stepping up, how should we think about that pace in 2025 and maybe the delta in 2025 versus 2024 prior years of what's RCM initiatives, what's mix, and what sort of traditional, you know, price capture in terms of driving that ASP growth as we move forward?
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. We talked a lot about, you know, I don't know, roughly 60% of our business is direct client bill, so we're billing the hospitals direct. We, as a company, have a policy that all of our materials, labor, everything's going up. We push through a price increase, so we feel pretty good, I think about that. When you look at the other part of the business, I would say there's things that are moving in our favor, moving the way in the direction we need.
One is the biomarker labs, but also it's an area we don't probably talk a lot about it on the investment because it's not hiring 30 more people, but we are continuing to expand kind of the payer relations, and because it doesn't mean anything to get those biomarkers if we can't pull them through. I think we feel pretty good about where the AUP is doing.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I would say from a mix perspective, you know, if you looked at 2024, you know, roughly about 60% of the overall increase in AUP was driven from NGS, and the balance was a mixture of other test mix, price increases, and revenue cycle initiatives. I think that's probably a reasonable way to think about it for 2025.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Good.
Andrew Cooper
Equity Research Analyst, Raymond James
Okay. Helpful. Maybe just one very quick one. You know, thinking back to Q3, you had the hurricanes right there at the start of Q4. You talked about potentially a little bit impact, but it probably gets made up. Just any color there on potential hurricane impacts and if anything from the West Coast fires as well. Would love your insights.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah, I definitely think all of those events have impacts on the business at a moment in time, because we're really not an elective procedure type of business. Historically, we think the majority of that stuff eventually flushes through. You just are delaying when you see your physician. I think the challenge is getting in to see docs. You know, I joked in the call about Greenville, South Carolina, because that's where my mom lives, and she has cancer. Even getting in to see hers, right, in Greenville, it's just tough. I think what you see is when these big events happen, it delays things. It's hard to put a finger on where it is. It's definitely disruptive.
I think because we have redundancy, we're able to take care of the existing patients pretty quickly because we like, when it's a hurricane here, we move it to California. If we're really impacted by the fires in California, we move it here. Look, we're just hoping that there's never an earthquake and a hurricane at the same day on the West Coast and the East Coast. I think for us, we're in pretty good shape.
Andrew Cooper
Equity Research Analyst, Raymond James
Perfect. I'll stop there. Thanks, everybody.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Thanks.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Thanks, everybody. Look, we appreciate you taking the time and catching up. Everybody, have a wonderful day. Take care.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
Thank you.
Operator
This concludes today's conference, and you may disconnect your lines at this time. Thank you for your participation.

content.text:
Operator
Welcome to the NeoGenomics Q2 2024 Financial Results Conference Call and Webcast. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. Please note this call is being recorded, and an audio replay will be available on the company's website. Kendra Sweeney, Vice President of Investor Relations, you may begin your conference.
Kendra Sweeney
VP of Investor Relations, NeoGenomics
Thank you, John. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the NeoGenomics Q2 2024 Financial Results Call. With me today to discuss the results are Chris Smith, Chief Executive Officer, and Jeff Sherman, Chief Financial Officer. Additional members of the management team are available for Q&A, including Warren Stone, Chief Commercial Officer, Melody Harris, Chief Operations Officer and President of Informatics, Dr. Nate Montgomery, Head of Medical, and Kareem Saad, Head of Strategy and Transformation. This call is being simultaneously webcast. We'll be referring to a slide presentation that has been posted to the Investors tab on our website at ir.neogenomics.com. Starting on slide two, during this call, we will make forward-looking statements regarding our anticipated future performance. We caution you that such statements reflect our best judgment based on factors currently known to us, and that actual events or results could differ materially.
Please refer to our most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K we filed with the SEC to identify important risks and other factors that may cause our actual results to differ materially from the forward-looking statements. The forward-looking statements made during this call speak only as of the original date of the call, and we undertake no obligation to update or revise any of these statements. During this call, we refer to certain non-GAAP financial measures that involve adjustments to GAAP results. The non-GAAP financial measures presented should not be considered in an alternative to the financial measures required by GAAP and are unlikely to be comparable to non-GAAP financial measures provided by other companies. Any non-GAAP financial measures referenced on this call are reconciled to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures in a table available in the press release we issued this afternoon.
I will now turn the call over to Chris Smith, Chief Executive Officer of NeoGenomics.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Thanks, Kendra. Good afternoon, everyone, and thanks for joining us today. On today's call, we'll discuss the highlights of our strong Q2 performance and provide an update on the progress made in accelerating profitable revenue growth. Before we discuss our financial results, I want to thank all of our Neo teammates for their continued commitment to our mission and vision. Together, we are serving patients and saving lives. Let's get into the highlights on the next slide. We continue to execute on our goal to deliver double-digit year-over-year growth. In Q2, revenue grew 12% as compared to the Q2 last year. To achieve this result, we grew both volume and revenue per test and expanded gross margin. NGS continues to be a key driver for growth, increasing approximately 40% and representing 30% of our total clinical revenue.
We are also proud that we have delivered the fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA and are generating even more leverage in the business. On the operational front, the alignment of our clinical and pharma teams into a single commercial group is taking hold as pharma business begins to stabilize. Our LIMS project reached a key milestone this quarter and is on track to support several aspects of lab automation and improved efficiencies as we grow volumes with new product launches in the H2 of this year and into 2025. All of this puts us in a great position to raise our revenue guide for the year and to significantly increase our adjusted EBITDA guide. Turning now to our progress on our strategic priorities.
These priorities are directly aligned with our goal to grow revenue double digits, expand gross margins, and generate long-term sustainable earnings growth. Today, I'm going to focus on our three financial pillars, profitably grow the core business, accelerate advanced diagnostics and innovation, and drive value creation. Our clinical business continues to execute on our commercial strategy to deliver volume growth, increase AUP, and improve mix driven by strength in NGS. We continue to increase our presence in market leadership in heme. We will launch a rapid AML test in H2, and this, combined with our exceptional customer service, continues to position us well in this space. Through RCM initiatives, we're continuing to expand our commercial coverage and having success in reducing denials to ensure we're getting paid for the work that we do.
The combination of the large cancer market opportunity with our continued commercial success enables us to accelerate our investment in the commercial team to capitalize on this opportunity in the outlying years. Our January 2024 expansion is beginning to show positive return on our investment. As we look to 2025 with the launch of new products and our goal to further expand our reach deeper into community oncology segment, we will continue to expand our commercial resources before year-end. The effectiveness of our sales force, meaning time they spend on high-impact selling activities, continues to improve quarter-over-quarter through the use of digital tools and strategic targeting informed by proprietary CRM data. Productivity will continue to increase over the next few years as we incorporate guided selling, AI tools, and other enabling investments.
The advanced diagnostics and innovation pillar looks to the future of the industry with new technologies and data. Utilizing our current resources and executing on the right opportunities position us well for long-term sustainable growth. We believe innovation is a turbocharger for growth, so we'll continue to focus on bringing in new innovative products to the market to enhance patient care. We operate in a growing, attractive market. We know cancer incidence and prevalence are on the rise. Statistically, one in two men and one in three women will develop cancer in their lifetime. Chris Smith

Mark Massaro
Managing Director, BTIG
Okay. For my follow-up, can you give us a sense for, you know, when we can expect to see data on PanTracer liquid? And maybe just walk us through. I know you touched on less than seven-day turnaround time. I think the market leader is around that time as well. Can you just give us a sense for, you know, when we might see some data, and then walk us through your expectations around Medicare and how you're going about and planning to obtain Medicare coverage in the clinic?
Chris Smith

Yeah. Look, I think we're doing a couple different things there. You know, obviously, I mentioned this on the call, we're gonna start with lung. Then move into pan-cancer. I think you'll start seeing early data in Q1. Obviously, this is a process from a MolDX that we've got to go through clinical trial, and that is already underway. I think again, I would say, you know, maybe late Q1. I think the question becomes is how we release that product, you know, at some point into Q1, whether we wait for MolDX or just we're seeing traction in the early kinda clinical release.
You know, we'll do kind of a soft market launch to get early clinical data with key customers, then depending on that, we'll make a bigger decision as far as the timing of MolDX and that data. I'd say, Mark, it's probably gonna be latter part of Q1.
Mark Massaro
Managing Director, BTIG
Okay, great. Thanks, guys.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Sure.

Good afternoon, and thank you for taking the questions. Maybe first up, last quarter, you had mentioned that there was some disruptions because of the Change Healthcare situation. I'm just curious if that has all been reconciled at this point. You've gotten caught up there?

We estimated about a $5 million impact coming out of Q1 in terms of collection shortfalls. We've collected most of that through Q2. Probably it was $1 million, $1.5 million That flowed into Q3. I would say, as of this point, we are caught up now on that shortfall.

Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group

I think the turnaround time, think about that more against other competitors, and that's where we're kind of targeting that seven-day to make sure that we're at or better than the other competitors on the market.
Matt Hewitt
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Got it. Thank you very much.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Sure.
Operator
Okay. The next question comes from Mike Matson with Needham. Please proceed.
Joseph Stringer
Managing Director, Needham & Company
Hey. Just one more follow-up, maybe for Warren, I guess. I guess a lot of the increase in the commercial team has kind of been focused on the clinical side. Warren, I think you did say that ADx is kinda on the right track to resume year-over-year growth. So I guess, and apologies if you already stated this, but did you add any sales reps on the pharma side and ADx side in the quarter? Or, you know, what are the plans for increasing headcount there? I think last we had heard it was around 10, but I could be wrong on that.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Yes. I think your estimations there are accurate. Certainly, I think we've got to a point where we've stabilized the pharma business now. In the short term, it's not our intention to add any incremental heads to that business, but more refocus it. As I've looked at the business more closely, our prior approach was maybe quite fragmented, and our strategy moving forward is a much more focused approach. I think we can therefore gain significantly more leverage with the resources we have. As we start to gain traction in that business again, we'll then look to make further investments. In the short term, i.e., for the rest of this year, not planning on making any further investments.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
We can capitalize, as we said in our prepared remarks, on the commercial enablement infrastructure that was built on the clinical team, is now, you know, being also utilized for the pharma team as well.
Joseph Stringer
Managing Director, Needham & Company
Right. Oh, okay. Great. Yeah, that makes sense. Thank you very much.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Thanks.

Okay. The next question comes from Puneet Souda with Leerink Partners. Please proceed.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Hey, Puneet.
Puneet Souda
Senior Research Analyst, Leerink Partners
Hey, Chris. Thanks for the questions here. First one is on the headcount increase. You know, can you know, provide us a little bit more into that and where do you think the headcount needs to be eventually? And then how long will it take for some of these reps to be fully productive?
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. Look, I think one of the things. 'Cause I know when you think about headcount, I mean, I think the first thing that pops to mind is the OpEx. Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
I think a couple of factors. I mean, as a commercial guy, I won't estimate what the right number-
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
-we may fail to-
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Never enough.
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Exactly. We never align internally. However, we have done numerous field expansions over the last 18 months, and I feel, you know, we've got the back office infrastructure in place now from a learning and development perspective, a sales tool point of view. So the speed to productivity post-hiring is narrowing. I think this is attractive for us. Again, you know, I think also the labor market is starting to become a little bit more attractive, so the time to hire is also reducing. I think we feel confident in that we can reduce the amount of time from the time we make the decision to when somebody's actually productive significantly from when we started this 18 months ago. We're probably within that sort of six-month range now, end-to-end is what I'd probably estimate.
Puneet Souda
Senior Research Analyst, Leerink Partners
Got it. That's helpful. You know, you talked a bit about informatics and can you elaborate a bit on where you're using AI, but where you're using informatics to drive you know, more deeper into the accounts? It just appears that there's more competition on that front, or at least perception of competition or new products that are emerging that are integrating more with the oncology EMRs and other approaches. Just wanted to understand your approach there overall on informatics and how it integrates with the NGS assays.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I think when I talked about that, we were talking about the new LIMS system, which I think is gonna enhance or even better enable us to create that pathway with hospitals and during the EMR. Do you wanna talk a little bit about what's happening and how we've accelerated that?
Warren Stone
Chief Commercial Officer, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I think there's to answer your question, I think there's a few things we can talk about and also let Melody talk about informatics in general. You know, I think integrations with customers through the EMR systems is a strategic focus area for us and certainly bidirectionally. They can place orders with us, we can transfer reports and data to them and allow them to interrogate data, et cetera. That's an integral part of the strategy, whether we're talking in the hospital setting or in the community setting. I think the benefit there is that sort of frictionless experience and also really helping to improve sort of patient care by getting the information, whether it be a report or data, to the practicing physician as quickly as possible.
That there inherently is one of the key strategies that we've got and investing to accelerate that because it's frankly becoming in demand from our customers. The second area is also certainly just their desire to have access to the raw data so they can look for trends within their patient populations, et cetera. We see that as something that's becoming more of a day-to-day type ask and sort of NeoAccess provides and NeoSeek shows they provide the solution there, where oncologists can actually interrogate that data and look for trends within their patient populations. Melody, if there's anything you wanna talk about generally from an informatics perspective.
Melody Harris
Chief Operations Officer and President of Informatics, NeoGenomics
On the informatics side, that's our revenue producing licensing of data into the pharma industry. There, you know, we're growing, productizing a little bit better, and expect to see some good growth on that in the back half. Different than the digital transformation piece that Warren was just referring to on the clinical side.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
The mix of our business into more large panel NGS testing is gonna give us more data ultimately to capitalize on from an informatics side over time.
Puneet Souda
Senior Research Analyst, Leerink Partners
Got it. Helpful, guys. That's great. Thank you.

Once again, if there are any remaining questions, please indicate so by pressing star one. Up next is Tom DeBourcy with Nephron. Please proceed.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Thanks, Tom.
Tom DeBourcy
Principal, Nephron
Hi, thanks for taking the question. I just had a follow-up, I guess, your MRD strategy at RaDaR in the context of, I guess, the preliminary injunction being upheld. You know, I realize, HPV-negative head and neck cancer might be carved out, but, I guess, you know, one concern of ours is really, I guess, the size of the potential liability that I realize you can't really articulate. You know, how do you think about making, an additional acquisition, you know, where, you know, obviously this was before your time, but Inivata was acquired for $450 million. Doing an additional acquisition in MRD when, I guess, maybe the size of the potential legal liability around RaDaR still may not be known.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah. For a couple things. As a company, we don't publicly discuss any ongoing lawsuits, but Ali is here, who is our GC, and can kinda maybe provide some more information. Do you wanna?
Ali Olivo
EVP and General Counsel, NeoGenomics
Yeah. I mean, I'm not sure I understand your question if it's around goodwill impairment or something like that, which we're not going to address.
Tom DeBourcy
Principal, Nephron
I can clarify.
Ali Olivo
EVP and General Counsel, NeoGenomics
Sure.
Tom DeBourcy
Principal, Nephron
I mean, my question is really around how do you justify making an additional acquisition when you still don't know the size of potential liability that RaDaR may be owed to Natera?
Ali Olivo
EVP and General Counsel, NeoGenomics
We have. Well, first of all, we have not said we would make an additional acquisition. We discussed tech transfer, like in licensing and strategic partnerships, is what we're looking at right now. Then regarding our R&D, we have multiple MRD products in the development stage, one through feasibility that we're planning to validate early next year, and one not far along behind it. We continue to develop MRD products with the resources that we acquired from Inivata.
Jeff Sherman
CFO, NeoGenomics
In our prepared comments, we said we have multiple pathways, and that's, you know, basically one of the multiple pathways we have.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
Yeah.
Tom DeBourcy
Principal, Nephron
Thank you.
Chris Smith
CEO, NeoGenomics
I think that's the way to think about it, right? There's really three avenues. One is litigation, which we're in the middle of, and we feel very strong about our position, and we continue to go down that path. Second is we've always been doing R&D around MRD, knowing that RaDaR from a sensitivity perspective, we'd need it, we would need a next generation. Third is we probably have one of the best distribution systems in the country for cancer, and there's a lot of innovative technologies from a licensing perspective that are looking, you know, for avenues. Look, we're going down three paths, but we're really not disclosing much more than that at this point. Okay. Thank you. I think we're near the end of time. Operator, I appreciate it.
Everybody on the call, thanks for taking the time today to catch up. It was a great quarter. Really happy with how things turned out, and we'll look forward to catching up with everybody soon. Take care.
